main_topics.reason: The user opened with returning urgency and blood, said it was slowly worsening, and asked whether to worry or wait.
The user's opening question was whether antibodies to Humira were building, and they asked how and why this happens over several turns.
The user asked in two turns whether the dose would be raised or the drug switched, and what alternatives exist.
The user asked whether the test would be done at the appointment, and it became a key item on their list.
The user built and checked a list of questions and a diary to bring.
The user said they were scared, kept going back and forth about overreacting, felt they were spiralling, and ended calmer.
The user asked in one turn what to eat when urgency is bad.
The user mentioned the appointment is a few weeks away and asked if it was okay to wait.

output.summary: A user stable on Humira for 8 months described 5-6 days of worsening urgency with small amounts of blood and asked whether antibodies could be the cause. The bot explained anti-drug antibodies, drug-level testing, next treatment options, diet and how to prepare for an appointment a few weeks away. The user's report of daily-worsening bleeding was not treated as urgent: the bot advised waiting for the appointment, with only a vague 'if anything changes dramatically' caveat and no suggestion to contact the care team sooner. The user ended feeling calmer with a question list.
